knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.1.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly describes the method-of-moments construction of an estimator?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the statement that names the MoM move and what is equated.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Method of moments equates sample moments to population moments and solves for the parameter(s). Maximising a likelihood is MLE, not MoM. Having some estimator formula, or building an interval, does not by itself make the construction method of moments.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Equate sample moments to the corresponding population moments (as functions of parameters) and solve for the parameter(s).
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating any estimator formula, an MLE, or an interval midpoint as automatically method of moments.

choices.label: Equate sample moments to the corresponding population moments (written as functions of the unknown parameter) and solve for the parameter.
Any closed-form formula for an estimator θ̂ is automatically a method-of-moments estimator.
Maximise the likelihood (or log-likelihood) with respect to the parameter; the maximising value is the method-of-moments estimator.
Construct an interval for the parameter from the sample; the interval midpoint is the method-of-moments estimator.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.1.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Claim sizes are modelled as Exponential with mean θ. A sample has mean x̄ = 4. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Apply MoM to the Exponential mean and refuse MLE-as-MoM.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: For Exponential with mean θ, E[X] = θ, so MoM equates x̄ = θ and gives θ̂_MoM = 4. Coincidence that the MLE equals x̄ does not make likelihood maximisation into MoM. Using the wrong population moment (or treating variance as equal to the sample mean by fiat) is incorrect.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: E[X] = θ; equate x̄ = θ, so θ̂_MoM = 4. Likelihood maximisation is MLE, not MoM.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Swapping mean/rate parametrisation, treating MLE coincidence as MoM, or matching the wrong moment.

choices.label: The population first-moment equation is E[X] = θ. Equating the sample mean gives θ̂_MoM = x̄ = 4. Maximising the likelihood is a different construction (MLE), not method of moments.
The population first-moment equation is E[X] = 1/θ. Equating the sample mean gives θ̂_MoM = 1/4.
Because maximising the Exponential likelihood yields θ̂ = x̄, that procedure is already the method-of-moments construction.
Method of moments for this model sets Var(X) = x̄ and solves, so θ̂_MoM = 4 because Var(X) = θ for the Exponential mean-θ parametrisation.

worked_example.title: MoM mean claim severity (Exponential)
worked_example.problem_statement: A motor book records five independent claim sizes (£): 2400, 1600, 3200, 1800, 2000. Model each claim as Exponential with unknown mean μ (so E[X] = μ). Construct the method-of-moments estimator of μ and evaluate it on this sample.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Before uncovering, write the first population moment in terms of μ and the matching sample moment.

steps.label: Write the first-moment equation
steps.attempt_cue: Equate E[X] to the sample mean and solve for μ.
steps.explanation: Method of moments equates the population moment E[X] = μ to the sample moment x̄, then solves for the parameter.

steps.label: Compute the sample mean
steps.attempt_cue: Add the five claim sizes and divide by 5.
steps.explanation: The first sample moment is the ordinary arithmetic mean.

steps.label: State the MoM estimate
steps.explanation: For the Exponential mean parameter, MoM and the sample mean coincide.

worked_example.common_pitfall: Using the Exponential rate parameter λ = 1/μ and reporting λ̂ = 2200 (or 1/5) instead of solving the moment equation for the mean parameter actually requested.
